taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM ET (Eastern Time) on September 30, 2026 to Madrid time.

ET (Eastern Time) is UTC-4 during daylight saving time in September.
Madrid is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+2 during daylight saving time in September.

The time difference is 6 hours, with Madrid being ahead of ET.

5:00 PM ET = 17:00 ET
Adding 6 hours: 17:00 + 6:00 = 23:00 Madrid time

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert UTC time to Lima, Peru time.

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time zone (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru doesn't observe daylight saving time).

The deadline is July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC.

To convert from UTC to Lima time, I subtract 5 hours:
12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00 Lima time

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from CEST (Central European Summer Time) to Japan Standard Time (JST).

CEST is UTC+2, and JST is UTC+9, so JST is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

The deadline is June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST.
Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM gives us 4:00 PM (16:00) in JST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) to Madrid time (Central European Time).

PDT is UTC-7, while Madrid is UTC+2 (CEST during summer) or UTC+1 (CET during winter).

On October 11, 2026, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1) since it will be after the end of daylight saving time in Europe (which ends on the last Sunday of October, October 25, 2026).

So the time difference is 8 hours (from UTC-7 to UTC+1).

11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 PDT
Adding 8 hours: 23:59 + 8 hours = 07:59 the next day

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST to Madrid time.

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8, while Madrid (CET/CEST) is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer. 

In March 2026, Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2) since daylight saving time typically starts in late March.

So PST to CEST is a 10-hour difference (PST is 8 hours behind UTC, CEST is 2 hours ahead of UTC, so 8+2=10 hours).

March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST + 10 hours = March 4, 2026 at 9:59 AM CEST

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 09:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 10:00 AM CET (Central European Time) on February 2, 2026 to Los Angeles time.

CET is UTC+1, and Los Angeles is UTC-8 (PST) or UTC-7 (PDT) depending on the time of year. In February, Los Angeles is on PST (UTC-8).

So the conversion is:
- 10:00 AM CET = 10:00 AM UTC+1
- This equals 09:00 UTC (subtract 1 hour)
- 09:00 UTC = 01:00 AM PST (subtract 8 hours)

Since February 2, 2026 is in winter, Los Angeles will be on PST.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 8:00 AM JST (Japan Standard Time) on May 5, 2026 to Lima, Peru time.

JST is UTC+9, and Lima, Peru is UTC-5 (Peru does not observe daylight saving time).

The time difference is 14 hours, with Lima being 14 hours behind Japan.

8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 converts to 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026 in Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Pacific Time (PT) to Madrid time.

Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-8 in winter and UTC-7 in summer. Since October 28, 2026 will be in winter, PT will be UTC-8.

Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer. Since October 28, 2026 will be in winter, Madrid will be UTC+1.

The time difference is 9 hours (UTC-8 to UTC+1).

11:59 PM PT = 23:59 PT
Adding 9 hours: 23:59 + 9 hours = 08:59 the next day

So 11:59 PM PT on October 28, 2026 becomes 8:59 AM on October 29, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Eastern Time (ET) to Madrid time.

Eastern Time (ET) is UTC-5 (or UTC-4 during daylight saving time). Spain uses Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+1 (or UTC+2 during daylight saving time).

On October 30, 2026:
- ET will be in standard time (EST = UTC-5)
- Spain will be in standard time (CET = UTC+1)
- This means Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET

9:00 AM ET + 6 hours = 3:00 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 18:00 CET (Central European Time) on October 27, 2026 to New York time.

CET is UTC+1, and New York is typically UTC-4 (Eastern Time) during this period of the year.

So I need to subtract 5 hours from the CET time:
18:00 CET - 5 hours = 13:00 New York time

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Pacific Time (PT) to Madrid time.

PT (Pacific Time) is UTC-8 in winter and UTC-7 in summer. Madrid is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer.

On November 2, 2026, we need to check if daylight saving time is in effect:
- Spain ends DST on the last Sunday of October, so November 2nd will be in standard time (UTC+1)
- California (PT) ends DST on the first Sunday of November, so November 2nd will still be in daylight saving time (UTC-7)

So the time difference is 8 hours (UTC-7 to UTC+1).

11:59 PM PT = 23:59 PT
Adding 8 hours: 23:59 + 8 hours = 07:59 the next day

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Pacific Time (PT) to Madrid time.

March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT needs to be converted to Madrid time. During this period, Pacific Time will be in PDT (Pacific Daylight Time, UTC-7) and Madrid will be in CEST (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2).

The time difference is 9 hours, with Madrid being ahead of Pacific Time.

11:59 PM PDT + 9 hours = 8:59 AM the next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from CET (Central European Time) to PST/PDT (Pacific Time in Los Angeles).

March 25, 2026 is in the spring, so Los Angeles will be on PDT (Pacific Daylight Time).

CET is UTC+1, and PDT is UTC-7, so there's an 8-hour difference.
When it's 12:00 PM CET, it's 4:00 AM PDT (8 hours earlier).

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 AM ET (Eastern Time) on October 12, 2026 to Madrid time.

12:00 AM ET means midnight at the start of October 12, 2026, in Eastern Time (US).

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET/CEST). In October, Spain is on CET (UTC+1) while the US Eastern Time is EDT (UTC-4) during daylight saving time.

The time difference is 5 hours, with Madrid being ahead of Eastern Time.

So when it's 12:00 AM (00:00) on October 12 in ET, it's 5:00 AM (05:00) on October 12 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 05:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) means the deadline is 23:59 on October 9, 2026 in the latest time zone on Earth, which is UTC-12 (Baker Island time). 

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET/CEST) zone, which is UTC+1 (or UTC+2 during daylight saving time). In October, Spain will be on UTC+2.

So I need to convert 23:59 UTC-12 to Madrid time (UTC+2):
- From UTC-12 to UTC+2 is a difference of 14 hours
- 23:59 + 14 hours = 13:59 the next day

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 PM PT (Pacific Time) on August 14, 2026 to Madrid time.

Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-7 during summer (PDT). Madrid, Spain is in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

The time difference is 9 hours, with Madrid being ahead of Pacific Time.

12:00 PM PT = 21:00 (9:00 PM) CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from IST (Indian Standard Time) to CET/CEST (Central European Time, which is Madrid's time zone).

IST is UTC+5:30
Madrid (Spain) is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer

Since November 10, 2026 will be in winter (Spain switches to winter time on the last Sunday of October), Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

The time difference is: IST (UTC+5:30) - CET (UTC+1) = 4.5 hours ahead

So when it's 11:59 PM IST in India, it's 7:29 PM CET in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Nepal time (UTC+5:45) to Lima, Peru time (UTC-5).

The time difference is 10 hours and 45 minutes between Nepal and Lima.

When it's 5:00 PM in Nepal, it would be 6:15 AM in Lima (10 hours and 45 minutes earlier).

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Adelaide, Australia time to Madrid, Spain time.

Adelaide is in Australian Central Standard Time (ACST, UTC+9:30) or Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT, UTC+10:30) depending on the date. Since October is spring in the Southern Hemisphere, Adelaide will be on ACDT (UTC+10:30).

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) or Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). In October, Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2) since Spain typically switches to winter time in late October or early November.

The time difference is: ACDT (UTC+10:30) to CEST (UTC+2) = 8.5 hours behind.

10:00 AM in Adelaide = 1:30 AM in Madrid (same day).

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Sydney time to Madrid time for the deadline of 6:00 PM on October 3, 2026.

Sydney, Australia is in Australian Eastern Time (AEST/AEDT), which is UTC+10/+11.
Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+1/+2.

In October, Sydney will be on AEDT (UTC+11) and Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2).
This means Sydney is 9 hours ahead of Madrid.

When it's 6:00 PM in Sydney, it will be 9 hours earlier in Madrid.
6:00 PM - 9 hours = 9:00 AM

Since October 3rd in Sydney corresponds to October 3rd in Madrid (both are in the same calendar date), the deadline in Madrid local time will be:

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00
